text:
Stephanie Nguyen: Anyone have the latest approved language for incident notification? Getting pushed by Northbridge on “breach notification within 24 hours” + they want a definition of breach to paste into their questionnaire.

Lukas Meyer: +1. EMEA prospect (HelioFin) asking specifically: “What constitutes a Security Incident vs Personal Data Breach?” and “When do you notify customers?” Need something we can copy/paste that won’t get us in trouble.

Jordan Blake: Please drop the canonical wording here. We keep getting different answers in email threads.

Markus Klein: From SE side: we need a short answer for RFPs and a longer one for when Legal gets involved. Also please include where to route if they insist on a hard SLA.

Naomi Feldman: Yup. Sharing the Security/GRC-approved boilerplate (safe for questionnaires). Important: do not commit to specific hours unless it’s in the executed agreement (MSA/DPA). Use this verbatim.

Naomi Feldman: ---
Approved language (customer questionnaire / RFP):
“Redwood Inference maintains an incident response program with defined procedures for detection, triage, containment, eradication, and recovery. If Redwood becomes aware of a Security Incident impacting Customer Data, Redwood will notify the customer without undue delay in accordance with the terms of the applicable agreement and any applicable law. Notifications are provided through the customer’s designated security/compliance contacts and will include information reasonably necessary to support the customer’s response, such as the nature of the incident, impacted systems/data (to the extent known), and remediation steps taken.”

Naomi Feldman: Definitions snippet (use when they ask “what is a breach?”):
“‘Security Incident’ generally refers to unauthorized access to, acquisition of, or disclosure of Customer Data, or material loss of availability of systems processing Customer Data, as further defined in the parties’ agreement. A ‘Personal Data Breach’ (or similar term) refers to a security incident involving personal data as defined by applicable privacy law (e.g., GDPR).”
---

Olga Petrov: Adding GRC caveat: please avoid “always” / “within X hours” unless it’s contract language. If they insist on 24/48/72 hours, route to Legal + GRC for redlines. Also, if they reference GDPR 72 hours: that obligation applies to controllers notifying regulators; our customer notifications are governed by the DPA terms.

Marcus Lin: +1. Also please avoid saying “breach” unless the contract uses that term. We usually stick to “Security Incident” in customer-facing comms and only confirm “breach” if we’ve done full triage and Legal is aligned.

Stephanie Nguyen: Super helpful. Can we add a line about where they can see updates (status page etc.)? They asked “how will we know?”.

Naomi Feldman: Yep, approved add-on line (optional):
“During an active incident, Redwood will provide periodic updates via direct communications to the customer’s designated contacts and, where appropriate, via Redwood’s status page for service-impacting events.”

Lukas Meyer: Do we have a standard response for “Do you provide root cause analysis (RCA)?”

Marcus Lin: We can say “post-incident summary” but don’t promise a formal RCA for every event. Suggested phrasing:
“Following resolution of a material Security Incident, Redwood will provide a post-incident summary upon request, subject to confidentiality and security considerations.”

Daniel Carter: For evidence requests tied to this (IR policy, SOC 2, etc.) please route through the evidence process. Don’t attach SOC 2 report in email unless NDA is confirmed. If needed, I can turn around access once we have the requester + company + NDA status.

Markus Klein: Perfect. Naomi — can you confirm this matches what’s going into the Security FAQ v2 / RFP library so we don’t fork language?

Naomi Feldman: Confirmed. This is the same wording going into the Security FAQ v2 and the standardized RFP response library. If you see variants floating around, ping me and I’ll correct at the source.

Jordan Blake: Great. Stephanie/Lukas: please use this and route hard timeline demands to Naomi + Olga + Legal. Thank you.

Stephanie Nguyen: :thumbsup: Will use verbatim.

Lukas Meyer: :thumbsup: Thanks all.
